Degeneracy and caveats: Main route for sulfide oxidation. On its own, oxidation stops at S0.
Alternative to sqr; some strains carry both.

A complete system (soxABCDXYZ) oxidises thiosulfate directly to sulfate without releasing S0. soxCD-deficient (K17225) strains accumulate extracellular S0, which can be cross-checked against wording such as "oxidation ... to sulfate" in the literature.

Most important degeneracy: sulfate reduction (reductive type) and sulfur oxidation (reverse rDsr) share the same KO. Resolve by (1) placement in a dsrAB reference tree, (2) presence of dsrEFH (oxidative direction only), (3) QmoABC (reductive) vs AprM (oxidative).
Retained only in the oxidative direction; the decisive evidence for calling dsrAB direction.
Fully shared with sulfate reducers (degenerate). Apply the same criteria as for dsrAB.
Direct sulfite oxidation; a route separate from aprAB+sat.

Nearly indistinguishable in sequence from trithionate hydrolase; substrate specificity is hard to resolve even with an HMM. Polythionates are intermediates that feed into the sox or rDsr systems, so energetically they belong with thiosulfate.
Produces tetrathionate from thiosulfate; doxDA acts similarly.
Requires a custom HMM. Nitrogen is released during degradation.
Downstream of route B. Strains carrying it may not need a separate nitrogen source, which matters for medium design.

Most important degeneracy: shares its KOs with pmoABC (methane monooxygenase). Resolve by sequence phylogeny, taxonomy, and presence of hao. Being a monooxygenase, O2 is a substrate itself, so the acceptor is aerobic even when the paper does not say so.
Present in AOB, absent in AOA. Decisive marker, and it tracks the CO2-fixation split (AOB = CBB, AOA = 3-HP/4-HB).

Most important degeneracy: shares its KOs with narGH (nitrate reduction, the reverse reaction). Resolve by localisation signal (Tat), subunit composition, and phylogenetic placement; cytoplasmic vs periplasmic orientation varies by genus.
Nitrospira may carry both amo and nxr (comammox); always check.
KOs do not distinguish uptake from evolving hydrogenases. Classify with HydDB or the group-specific HMMs in METABOLIC. Group 1 membrane-bound enzymes are the uptake type.
Common in anaerobes; direction again resolved with HydDB.
F420-dependent and electron-bifurcating types in methanogenic archaea; form complexes with Hdr.
Principal marker for neutrophilic FeOB (Gallionella, Mariprofundus). Not detectable via KEGG.
Sideroxydans and relatives; highly similar to mtrAB.
Reported for photoferrotrophic iron oxidation; limited relevance to chemolithoautotrophy.

Acidophilic FeOB (Acidithiobacillus, Leptospirillum). Note these are electron-transfer proteins rather than the oxidising enzyme itself. Some are proposed to run in reverse for Fe(III) reduction under anaerobic conditions.
Form I vs Form II is decided by the AYXCSFR motif (Form I is the high-affinity type); the KO alone does not tell them apart.
Co-localised with acsB of the WL pathway. In the anaerobic type CO serves as both donor and carbon source (incorporated as the carbonyl group by ACS).
A frequent alternative to H2. Presence of the gene does not guarantee growth, so cross-check against negative substrate lists in the literature.
Variant forms including tungsten-dependent enzymes.
Shares its KOs with amoABC. Resolve by taxonomy (Verrucomicrobiota vs Pseudomonadota) and sequence phylogeny. Being a monooxygenase, O2 is a substrate itself.
Alternative enzyme expressed under low copper.
Positive indicates the autotrophic type (Methylacidiphilum, set No.26); negative indicates a methylotrophic type that is not autotrophic.
Absence indicates the autotrophic type; presence indicates the methylotrophic type in which CH4 also serves as the carbon source.
Strains carrying only XoxF and lacking MxaFI require rare-earth salts (CeCl3, LaCl3) at nM levels in the medium; cultures fail to start if this is overlooked.

Functional group: Scope: sulfur, ammonia, nitrite, hydrogen, iron, CO, formate and methane donors. Mn(II), As(III) and phosphite are outside this sheet because reports are sparse (see the Electron donors sheet).

Priority: Essential = indispensable for calling the physiotype; Alternative = a different route to the same function; Supporting = for checking substrate range or downstream steps. Rows marked Difficult or No need a custom HMM or a dedicated tool.
KOs for electron acceptors and CO2-fixation pathways are on their own sheets. A set call needs all three: donor, acceptor and fixation pathway.
KO identifiers are subject to revision; re-check against the current KEGG release before implementing a pipeline.
